subject: How to handle known removals of unmarked animals

messages.author: 86229585a7e8ee22
messages.subject: How to handle known removals of unmarked animals
parts: We are conducting a population estimate of wolves in Alaska using DNA-based capture-recapture methods. This past season was our 5th year and, as it turns out, the hunting/trapping season was shifted to earlier in the season and therefore coincided with our study period. Approximately 45 animals were removed by trapping or hunting from our study area during DNA sampling. Approximately 15 of them were ones that had been previously detected in our hair snares and harvest took place within 1 sampling occasion from the last detection. In those cases, it seems relatively straightforward to be able to mark those identified animals as a known removal (i.e., treat them as being removed at the last sampling occasion). However, that leaves around 30 animals that were known to have been removed but had not been previously identified. To complicate matters, hunter/trapper reporting of harvest location is not very precise, with location usually reported only to the scale of watershed, peninsula, or other large geographical feature. Timing of those harvests are only known to within a 2-week period. These removals potentially represent a very large proportion of the total number of animals in the study area (up to 30% of the previous year's population estimate). Is there something I can do to include these unmarked removals in the analysis?

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: How to handle known removals of unmarked animals
parts:
I think there's no snap answer. Properly, you need to allow for both the spatial and temporal distribution of removals, as you understand. This could in theory be done by interleaving sampling 'occasions' with two detector arrays of differing type (hair snare and hunting/removal), and coding all detections on the hunting array as removals. I know you have only approximate locations for removals, but they may still be better than nothing. The two detector arrays form one traps object with a vector-valued detector type. I would use the 'multi' detector type across a coarse grid across hunted areas for the removal phases, and also specify binary usage for each 'detector' to distinguish snare and hunting occasions. I cannot be 100% sure that 'secr' will handle this without trying it.
Murray

messages.author: 86229585a7e8ee22
messages.subject: Re: How to handle known removals of unmarked animals
parts:
Thanks, Murray. That makes a lot of sense to me. I've gotten the data formatted as suggested and have been able to make the trap and capture history objects without any errors. I had initially expected that the vector of detector types should equal the total number of detectors, but I quickly discovered that it needed to equal the number of occasions. I suppose this means that multiple detector types cannot be used during the same occasion?

When accounting for removals, what time period does the density (and derived population size) estimate represent? The value at the end of the study period after all the removals have been deducted?

Thanks again!

messages.subject: Re: How to handle known removals of unmarked animals
parts: I haven't thought out all the details, but I think a Bayesian alternative would be to have a latent density thinning process with a known number of removals in specific regions, assumed to be removed uniformly across each region.
